# Colors and Strokes

#### Course: Canvas Foundations

## Colors and Strokes

Every shape you have drawn so far is plain black. The canvas context has three style properties that change that: fillStyle controls fill color, strokeStyle controls outline color, and lineWidth controls how thick outlines are.

The important thing to know is that the canvas API is state-based. You set a style property first, then draw - the style applies to everything drawn after it until you change it again. If you call fillRect() before setting fillStyle, the shape draws in the default color (black).

For example,

```html
1<!DOCTYPE html>
2<html lang="en">
3    <head>
4        <meta charset="UTF-8">
5        <title>Canvas</title>
6        <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
7    </head>
8    <body>
9        <canvas id="gameCanvas" width="400" height="300">
10        </canvas>
11        <script src="script.js">
12        </script>
13    </body>
14</html>
```

```css
1*  {
2    margin: 0;
3    padding: 0;
4    box-sizing: border-box;
5}
6body  {
7    display: flex;
8    justify-content: center;
9    align-items: center;
10    height: 100vh;
11    background: #f0f0f0;
12}
13canvas  {
14    display: block;
15    border: 1px solid #ccc;
16    background: #fff;
17}
```

```javascript
1const canvas = document.getElementById("gameCanvas");
2const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
3ctx.fillStyle = "#e74c3c";
4ctx.fillRect(50, 50, 80, 25);
5ctx.fillRect(140, 50, 80, 25);
6ctx.fillRect(230, 50, 80, 25);
7ctx.fillStyle = "#3498db";
8ctx.fillRect(150, 260, 100, 12);
9ctx.fillStyle = "#222";
10ctx.beginPath();
11ctx.arc(200, 150, 10, 0, Math.PI * 2);
12ctx.fill();
13ctx.fillStyle = "#000";
14ctx.font = "18px Arial";
15ctx.fillText("Score: 0", 10, 25);
```

Here you can see Brick Breaker taking shape - red bricks, a blue paddle, a dark ball, and a score display. Each fillStyle assignment applies to every draw call that follows it until the next assignment. That is why setting fillStyle = "#3498db" only colors the paddle, not the bricks above it.

A good habit to build now. Always set your style right before the shape it belongs to. That way the color and the shape stay together in your code and are easy to update later.

![Canvas showing colored bricks, paddle, ball, and score text with fillStyle labels](data:application/octet-stream;base64,)
